issue: Deathrattle _NythendraSplit reads source._nyth_remaining, which is stamped by _NythendraTrackHealth on EVERY SELF_DAMAGE event including the lethal hit. The broadcast in Damage.do fires AFTER target._hit(amount), so on the killing blow source.health <= 0 -> max(0, health) = 0. Thus _nyth_remaining == 0 at death and the deathrattle splits into 0 Beetles. Verified live: summoning Nythendra and dealing a lethal 7-damage Hit produces 0 Beetles. The unit test only kills it via nyth.destroy() (no damage event), which leaves the earlier non-lethal _nyth_remaining intact and masks the bug.
real: Printed: '[x]Taunt. Deathrattle: Split into 1/1 Beetles. At the start of your turn, reform with any remaining.' It should split into a number of 1/1 Beetles equal to its remaining Health when it died (e.g. ~3 Beetles if killed at 3 Health). In real play (combat/spell damage) it currently splits into nothing.

issue: _UrsocResurrect summons each killed minion under its ORIGINAL controller (Summon(ctrl, cid) where ctrl = the minion it killed's owner). Verified live: Ursoc kills two enemy minions, dies, and resurrects them back on the ENEMY's board (p2 field), not Ursoc's owner's board. Resurrection effects in Hearthstone always summon under the resurrector's control.
real: Printed: 'Battlecry: Attack ALL other minions. Deathrattle: Resurrect any this killed.' The resurrected minions should appear on Ursoc's owner's side of the board, not on the side of whoever originally owned them.

issue: _RiteDarkGift spends 2 Corpses and applies a fixed +2/+2 enchant (EDR_811e, a @custom_card not in data) as 'Dark Gift'. Dark Gift is a real EDR keyword: it grants one of a defined pool of distinct enchant effects (often offered as a choice / random gift), not a flat +2/+2.
real: Printed: 'Discover an Undead. Spend 2 Corpses to give it a Dark Gift.' Dark Gift is a generic-keyword approximation here (flat +2/+2); the real Dark Gift pool/choice is not modelled. (Set-wide known approximation.)

issue: _LeechSteal uses a hardcoded base of 2 plus the count of friendly Hideous Husks. The base steal value is the '@' placeholder in the token text (TAG_SCRIPT_DATA_NUM_1 = 1 is the per-Husk increment scaling reference, not the base). Base 2 is a best-fidelity guess matching the printed 'Hideous Husk adds +1 each' wording.
real: Printed token: 'At the end of your turn, your hero steals @ Health from the lowest Health enemy.' Husk: 'Your Leeches steal 1 more Health from their victims.' The @-base magnitude is a guess (best-fidelity = 2); flag per the set-wide Imbue/@-scaling note.

issue: _FalricDouble bumps controller.corpses_doubled on play and _FalricUndouble decrements it on deathrattle only. If Falric leaves play without a death (silence, bounce-to-hand, transform), the deathrattle never fires and the corpse-doubling stays stuck on. Also corpses_doubled only doubles minion-death corpse gains (the gate in actions.py:618); any non-minion-death corpse source would not be doubled.
real: Printed: 'You gain twice as many Corpses as normal. Battlecry: Draw a card that spends Corpses.' Should stop doubling when Falric leaves play by any means, and double all Corpse gains.

issue: play = _JumpscareDiscover(...).then(Give(CONTROLLER, Discover.CARD)) discovers a Demon costing 5+ and shuffles the unchosen two into the deck, but it does NOT attach any Dark Gift to the discovered demon. It never calls the shared _GiveDarkGift helper (neutral.py) that sibling EDR cards use (e.g. they do `.then(Give(...).then(_GiveDarkGift(Give.CARD)))`). So the entire Dark Gift portion of the card is missing, not merely approximated. The in-file comment acknowledges it: 'the Dark Gift attachment is a cross-class mechanic handled elsewhere' - but nothing applies it here.
real: Printed (EDR_882): 'Discover a Demon that costs (5) or more with a Dark Gift. Shuffle the other two into your deck.' The discovered demon must receive a (random) Dark Gift enchant; other EDR cards model this via _GiveDarkGift, Jumpscare grants none.

issue: _ResurrectAndCopy.do resurrects the *actual* dead graveyard card via Summon(player, card) (alongside a fresh base-stat clone via player.card(card.id)). Summon.do only sets card.zone = Zone.PLAY for a graveyard card without explicitly resetting damage/enchantments, so the resurrected original could in principle re-enter PLAY carrying residual state instead of as a clean base-stat copy. This is the engine's established resurrect pattern, so likely fine (zone-entry resets stats), but worth confirming the resurrected minion returns at full health with no leftover enchants. Selectors are otherwise correct: Felhunter COST<=4 (cost-5 self auto-excluded); Felbat COST>=5 - SELF honoring 'a different minion'.
real: Printed EDR_891: 'Deathrattle: Resurrect a friendly Deathrattle minion that costs (4) or less. Summon a copy of it.' EDR_892: 'Resurrect a different friendly Deathrattle minion that costs (5) or more. Summon a copy of it.' Resurrect should yield a clean copy (base stats, full health); 'a copy of it' adds one more identical minion = two total, which the impl produces.

issue: events = Play(CONTROLLER, NATURE_SPELL).after(_GroveShaperSummon(SELF, Play.CARD)). The .after trigger does not fire when the cast Nature spell's play opens a Discover/choice (which suspends the action queue). Verified at runtime: with Grove Shaper in play, casting Photosynthesis (EDR_848, no Discover) summons a 2/2 Treant, but casting Horn of Plenty (EDR_270, a Nature spell that Discovers) summons NO Treant. Repro: play Photosynthesis -> 1 treant; then play Horn of Plenty -> still 1 treant (the Horn cast was silently missed).
real: Printed: 'After you cast a Nature spell, summon a 2/2 Treant with "Deathrattle: Get a copy of that spell."' Horn of Plenty is a Nature spell (spell_school=NATURE/4), so casting it should summon a Treant. The only collectible Druid Nature spell that Discovers is Horn of Plenty, so the missed-trigger window is narrow but real.

issue: Hamuul imbues the Druid Hero Power, installing EDR_847p (Blessing of the Golem) from tokens.py. Its activate() summons a Plant Golem with stat = 2*level (L1=2/2, L2=4/4, L3=6/6 ...). This @-scaling magnitude is a best-fidelity guess.
real: Printed: 'Summon a @/@ Plant Golem.' Live data exposes only TAG_SCRIPT_DATA_NUM_1=1 on EDR_847p and a 1/1 base token (EDR_847pt2); the per-imbue @ growth is not encoded in the data, so the 2*level progression is an engine guess (the set-wide Imbue Hero-Power @-scaling approximation flagged in tokens.py).

issue: update = Refresh(FRIENDLY_MINIONS + BEAST - SELF, buff="EDR_480e") where EDR_480e doubles the Attack stat (atk = lambda self,i: i*2). Models "deal double damage" as a permanent doubling of every other friendly Beast's Attack stat, and explicitly excludes SELF via '- SELF'.
real: Printed: 'Rush\nFriendly Beasts deal\ndouble damage.' Two gaps: (1) it doubles the Attack STAT (so a beast visually shows e.g. 6 Attack instead of 3) rather than doubling damage dealt at the point of dealing it, so non-attack beast damage (spell/deathrattle/triggered damage from a Beast source) is never doubled and the displayed stats are wrong; (2) the printed effect says 'Friendly Beasts' with no 'other', so it should include Goldrinn itself (a Beast), but '- SELF' excludes Goldrinn, leaving its own 9 Attack un-doubled.

card: Blessing of the Moon (referenced set-wide Imbue)
issue: activate() discovers a Priest card and applies Buff(cost=-level); comment explicitly notes the 'but is Temporary' downside is not modelled.
real: Printed: 'Choose a Priest minion or Priest spell to add to your hand. It costs (@) less, but is Temporary.' The engine has no Temporary-card lifetime, so the discovered card persists (no end-of-turn removal). Flagged as a set-wide approximation; relevant here because the Hunter file's Imbue chain shares the same tokens.py Imbue infrastructure.

issue: play = Destroy(TARGET), Draw(CONTROLLER)*3 with requirements only {REQ_TARGET_TO_PLAY, REQ_FRIENDLY_TARGET, REQ_MINION_TARGET}. The target is restricted to any friendly minion, NOT specifically a Wisp. A player can destroy any friendly minion (a big legendary, a buffed threat) to draw 3 cards.
real: Printed: 'Destroy a friendly Wisp to draw 3 cards.' The card may only target friendly Wisps (EDR_851t, the 1/1 token). The impl lets it sacrifice any friendly minion, which is strictly stronger / wrong-target. The Wisp-only targeting filter (by card id, since Wisp has no Race tag) is not modelled.

issue: Gives the two generated spells the in-data enchant EDR_874e (SPELLPOWER:1) via Buff on the held card. But the engine's get_spell_damage only aggregates board-minion spellpower + aura adjustments + next_spell_spellpower (player.spellpower iterates self.field); it never reads a SPELLPOWER tag on the cast spell card itself. So the +1 Spell Damage rider has zero effect when Moonfire/Starfire are later cast.
real: Printed: 'Get a Moonfire and a Starfire. Give them Spell Damage +1.' The Moonfire should deal 2 (not 1) and Starfire 6 (not 5) when cast. The two-spells-to-hand half is full-fidelity; the damage-boost half is a no-op. (Limitation is documented in-code.)

issue: Both rely on Imbue installing the Mage Imbued Hero Power EDR_851p (Blessing of the Wisp), whose @-scaling is computed dynamically as amount = imbue_level + 1 -> Summon 2/3/4 Wisps and deal 2/3/4 split damage (tokens.py). The actual per-tier magnitudes are not present in the card data (only one EDR_851p token exists), so these numbers are best-fidelity guesses, and imbue_level is the GLOBAL imbue count this game rather than per-this-power.
real: Printed EDR_851p: 'Summon @ Wisps. Deal $@ damage randomly split among all enemies.' The true tier values for @ are guessed (set-wide Imbue @-scaling approximation flagged in tokens.py). Wisprider's 'Imbue then trigger it' and Spirit Gatherer's 'Get a Wisp + Imbue' wiring is otherwise correct.

issue: EDR_260t.draw does `yield Summon(CONTROLLER, ExactCopy(SELF)); yield Reveal(SELF)`. The draw hook fires while the Illusion card is already in HAND (Draw.do moved it there at card.zone = Zone.HAND). The script summons a COPY of the token to the board but never removes/destroys SELF, so the original 4/5 Illusion card stays in the player's hand as a fully playable card. EDR_260t has no CASTS_WHEN_DRAWN data tag (tag 388 is None), so the engine's auto-Destroy+Battlecry path never runs either - nothing removes the hand copy.
real: Printed (EDR_260t 'Illusion'): 'Summoned When Drawn Taunt'. A Summoned-When-Drawn card should be put directly onto the board when drawn (i.e. removed from hand), summoning exactly one 4/5 Taunt Dragon. The current impl yields TWO things from drawing one Illusion: a summoned board minion AND a leftover Illusion card still sitting in hand - effectively doubling the value. Correct idiom is to summon SELF (and clear it from hand), not summon a copy while keeping the original.

issue: play = Morph(FRIENDLY_DECK + NEUTRAL, RandomCard(card_class=CardClass.DRUID)). `RandomCard` is RandomCardPicker with NO collectible=True default (only RandomCollectible/RandomMinion/RandomSpell inject collectible=True). Morph.get_target_args calls _eval_card on the picker with no collectible enforcement, so the transform pool is every Druid-class card in the build (1443 total; only 515 collectible). Each Neutral deck card can morph into a non-collectible token, hero power, enchant, or adventure card.
real: Printed (EDR_873): 'Battlecry: Transform all Neutral cards in your deck into random Druid ones.' 'Druid ones' means random COLLECTIBLE Druid cards. The picker needs collectible=True (use RandomCollectible(card_class=DRUID) or add collectible=True) so it can't roll the ~928 non-collectible Druid entries.

issue: start_of_game yields GainMana(CONTROLLER,5) + GainMana(OPPONENT,5). GainMana.get_target_args clamps to target.max_resources, and Player.max_resources = 10 (player.py:82) with _max_mana clamped to that (player.py:509). At start of game max_mana is 0, so +5 just sets each player to 5 usable crystals; the cap can never exceed 10 for the rest of the game. There is no modelling of a raised mana ceiling above 10.
real: Printed (EDR_000): 'Increase both players' maximum Mana by 5.' In Hearthstone this lifts the maximum-mana ceiling ABOVE the normal 10 (toward 15), letting both players ramp past 10. The engine's hard max_resources=10 cap means Ysera's signature beyond-10 ramp is lost; net effect is just 'both players gain 5 mana crystals now'. (Battlecry 'Gain 3 Mana Crystals' via GainMana(CONTROLLER,3) is fine.)

issue: events = OWN_TURN_END.on(Attack(SELF, RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS))). The standard Attack GameAction (actions.py:446) deals attack damage to the chosen minion only; it has no trample/excess-to-hero routing (the excess-damage path lives in a separate Hit variant at actions.py:2629, not used here).
real: Printed (EDR_453): 'At the end of your turn, attack a random enemy minion (excess damage hits the enemy hero).' The parenthetical excess-damage-hits-the-hero (a trample effect) is NOT modelled - overkill damage is wasted instead of carrying over to the enemy hero. Functionally the attack on a minion works, but the trample clause is missing.

card: Treacherous Tormentor, Creature of Madness, Raptor Herald, Nightmare Lord Xavius, Dreambound Raptor
issue: All Dark-Gift cards route through _GiveDarkGift, which calls roll_bonus_effects() and applies ONE random keyword from the eight-keyword Delve/Badlands Bonus-Effect pool (Taunt, Windfury, Divine Shield, Poisonous, Elusive, Rush, Lifesteal, Reborn) via SetTags. The real Dark Gift pool is not enumerated in data (single EDR_102t 'Dark Gift' spell whose description is literally 'Executes nightmare bonus'), so the actual gift options are approximated by a generic keyword grant.
real: Printed cards say 'with a Dark Gift' / 'give it a random Dark Gift'. The genuine Dark Gift pool is a distinct set of Nightmare enchants (stat buffs and on-attack/keyword effects), not the Delve eight-keyword set. Affected: EDR_102 (Treacherous Tormentor), EDR_105 (Creature of Madness), CORE_EDR_004/EDR_004 (Raptor Herald), EDR_856 (Nightmare Lord Xavius), EDR_849 (Dreambound Raptor 'random Bonus Effect'). Shape is faithful (always granted, random, strict upgrade) but the specific options differ - set-wide approximation.

card: Flutterwing Guardian, Bitterbloom Knight, Resplendent Dreamweaver, Malorne the Waywatcher
issue: Imbue your Hero Power is provided by the engine Imbue(CONTROLLER) action plus the per-game imbues_this_game counter; the Imbued-Hero-Power tokens' @-scaling magnitudes (e.g. Emerald Portal dragon cost = 2 + 2*level in tokens.py EDR_445pt3) are best-fidelity guesses, not data-derived.
real: Printed: 'Imbue your Hero Power' (EDR_800, EDR_852); EDR_860 gates on 'Imbued your Hero Power twice'; EDR_888 on 'Imbued your Hero Power 4 times'. The gating counter logic is correct, but the per-level @ scaling values of the imbued hero-power tokens are estimated. Set-wide approximation to flag (tokens.py).

issue: play = Summon(CONTROLLER, ExactCopy(SELF)). Only the 'summon a copy of this' half is modelled.
real: Printed (EDR_780): 'Battlecry: Summon a copy of this. One secretly dies when it takes damage.' The 'one secretly dies when it takes damage' downside is not implemented - both copies are real, independent minions that survive damage normally (code comment acknowledges this as cosmetic). It is a behavioural downside, not purely cosmetic: in-engine the player keeps both minions through damage when the real card would lose one.

issue: picker = RandomMinion(is_standard=None, custom_filter=lambda c: bool(c.tags.get(4065))) passed to Discover. Discover.get_target_args sees no 'card_class' in filters, so it applies the neutral+hero-class weighting on top of the custom filter (copy_with_weighting). The 11 Wild Gods (tag 4065) each belong to a different class, so the weighting biases the 3-card offer toward neutral/own-class Wild Gods rather than an even draw from all 11.
real: Printed (EDR_888): 'Discover a Legendary Wild God.' Confirmed 11 tag-4065 cards exist, all Legendary class minions (Ohn'ahra, Cenarius, Ursol, Omen, Aessina, Tortolla, Goldrinn, Agamaggan, Ashamane, Ursoc, Aviana). Pool identity is correct; only the per-class Discover weighting may skew which 3 are offered. The Cost-to-1 buff (EDR_888e cost=SET(1)) when imbues>=4 is correctly gated. Worth a defensive note.

issue: play = ChooseBoth(CONTROLLER) & ((Buff(SELF,"EDR_257ae"), SetTag(SELF, GameTag.DIVINE_SHIELD)), Buff(SELF,"EDR_257be")). When ChooseBoth is active (a 'play both Choose One options' enabler), the engine's trigger_actions iterates the branch tuple ((Buff,SetTag), Buff). The first element is itself a tuple, which has no .trigger attribute, so game.py:299 hits the 'Skipping non-Action' defensive branch and silently drops the entire Holy Bond branch. Result: under Choose-Both, Lightmender gets only +3 Health and Lifesteal, never the +3 Attack and Divine Shield. The normal Choose-One path is fine (sub-cards EDR_257a/b each have a flat play tuple).
real: Printed: 'Taunt. Choose One - +3 Attack and Divine Shield; or +3 Health and Lifesteal.' Under a Choose-Both effect the minion should receive BOTH halves: +3 Attack, Divine Shield, +3 Health and Lifesteal. Fix: flatten branch A to (Buff(SELF,"EDR_257ae"), SetTag(SELF, GameTag.DIVINE_SHIELD)) at the same nesting level, or wrap the two actions so each branch is a single action.

issue: Imbue(CONTROLLER) installs the Paladin Imbued Hero Power EDR_445p (Blessing of the Dragon), whose Emerald Portals summon @-Cost Dragons with @ scaled as dragon_cost = 2 + 2*level (L1=4, L2=6, L3=8) in tokens.py:27. These @-scaling values are best-fidelity guesses, not data-derived.
real: Printed EDR_445p: 'Shuffle two Emerald Portals into your deck. (Your Portals summon @-Cost Dragons.)' and EDR_445pt3: 'Casts When Drawn: Summon a random @-Cost Dragon.' The actual per-imbue-level Dragon cost progression is not encoded in the available CardXML and is approximated (4/6/8). Known set-wide Imbue @-scaling approximation.

issue: _TorethReinforce tracks per-minion _toreth_shield_hits and re-grants the shield (SetTag DIVINE_SHIELD) until 3 hits. The counter is per-minion lifetime and never resets. If a minion that already absorbed hits gains a brand-new Divine Shield from another source, the old hit count persists, so the new shield may break in fewer than 3 hits. Re-grant correctly works because card.py:1544 _hit checks both the divine_shield property and the DIVINE_SHIELD tag.
real: Printed: 'Divine Shield, Taunt. Your Divine Shields take three hits to break.' Mechanism is sound for a single shield; the non-reset counter across a minion's lifetime is a non-obvious edge case worth a defensive note. Also note the effect is implemented via events (torn down when Toreth leaves play), which correctly matches it being an in-play aura.

card: Blessing of the Moon (Priest Imbued Hero Power)
issue: activate() yields Discover(CONTROLLER, RandomCard(card_class=CardClass.PRIEST)). RandomCard applies only the card_class filter with NO collectible filter and NO type filter. The resolved pool (cards.filter(card_class=PRIEST)) is 801 cards: 332 minions, 360 spells, 105 HERO cards, 4 weapons, and 321 of them non-collectible (tokens/enchants). So the Discover can offer hero cards, weapons, and non-collectible junk.
real: Printed text (EDR_449p): 'Choose a Priest minion or Priest spell to add to your hand. It costs (@) less, but is Temporary.' The pool must be restricted to COLLECTIBLE Priest minions and Priest spells only -- should use weighted RandomCollectible(type=MINION,card_class=PRIEST) + RandomCollectible(type=SPELL,card_class=PRIEST), not bare RandomCard(card_class=PRIEST). NOTE: token lives in tokens.py but is the Priest Imbue payoff for EDR_449 Lunarwing Messenger and EDR_970 Kaldorei Priestess.

card: Blessing of the Moon (Priest Imbued Hero Power)
issue: The discovered card is given Buff(Give.CARD, 'EDR_449pe', cost=-level) and nothing else. The 'but is Temporary' downside is explicitly not modelled (code comment admits this). The card is added permanently and can be held across turns.
real: Printed text (EDR_449p): '...It costs (@) less, but is Temporary.' Temporary means the card is discarded at end of turn if not played. The impl drops this drawback entirely, so the card is strictly better than printed (permanent, full cost reduction, no expiry).

issue: play = None and no events/trigger wired. The _HarbingerSummon action exists but is never invoked by any real game event, so the card is completely inert in actual play. The only test that exercises the effect (test_harbinger_summons_two_two_cost_minions) calls _HarbingerSummon manually via game.cheat_action - no in-game path reaches it.
real: Printed (EDR_781): 'Whenever this enters your hand from the battlefield, summon two random 2-Cost minions.' The card should fire whenever it bounces from the board back to hand. The impl's own comment admits the bounce/zone-change trigger 'does not exist yet', so in a real game the minion never summons anything.

issue: EDR_525e1 (Corrupted Toxins) carries POISONOUS + TAG_ONE_TURN_EFFECT and is buffed onto the friendly weapon. But the end-of-turn one-turn-effect sweep in game.py iterates self.entities and player hands; Player.entities (player.py:604) yields field/secrets/buffs/hero/location/self but NOT player.weapon. So a one-turn buff on the weapon is never removed, and 'Poisonous this turn' becomes PERMANENT Poisonous. The impl comment acknowledges this as an engine gap, but the live behaviour is wrong.
real: Printed (EDR_525 Choose One first half / EDR_525A Extra Eyes): 'Gain Poisonous this turn.' Data tags on EDR_525e1: POISONOUS(330)=1, TAG_ONE_TURN_EFFECT(331)=1 - the Poisonous must fade at end of the current turn. In the engine it never fades.

issue: Combo path buffs the discovered copy with EDR_528e, a @custom_card enchant hardcoded to GameTag.ATK=1 / HEALTH=1 (a fixed +1/+1). Dark Gift is modelled as a flat stat boost rather than a random gift selected from the Dark Gift pool.
real: Printed (EDR_528): 'Discover a copy of a minion in your opponent's deck. Combo: With a Dark Gift.' A Dark Gift is a randomly-chosen powerful enchantment from a defined pool (set-wide keyword, e.g. used by EDR_102, EDR_856, EDR_811). The fixed +1/+1 is a best-fidelity stand-in; magnitude and effect variety do not match the real Dark Gift pool. (Set-wide known approximation.)

issue: _CopyLowestCostInEnemyHand resolves ties deterministically by leftmost (next(c for c in opp_hand if c.cost == lowest)) rather than randomly among the tied lowest-cost cards.
real: Printed (EDR_521): 'Get a copy of the lowest Cost card in your opponent's hand.' When several cards tie for lowest cost, Hearthstone picks one at random; the impl is deterministic-leftmost. Minor and usually unobservable, but not RNG-faithful.

issue: _ShadowcloakedShuffle shuffles ALL of the opponent's cards whose id matches any card in your hand (matches = every opp card with a shared id). If the wording is 'shuffle theirs' (singular, one matching card), this over-shuffles.
real: Printed (EDR_524): 'If you're holding one of the same cards as your opponent, shuffle theirs into their deck.' Wording is ambiguous on count; shuffling every matching copy is a plausible reading but worth confirming against the real card (it may shuffle only the one shared card).

issue: Class body is empty/inert (no play, events, or engine hook). The card is shipped as a plain 1/1/2 vanilla minion; the transform-upgrade rider is not wired (documented in a NOTE comment referencing Baroness Vashj REV_925).
real: Printed: 'If this would transform into a minion, it transforms into one that costs (2) more.' Live data carries TRIGGER_VISUAL=1, indicating an active replacement effect on transform/Morph that the impl does not implement.

issue: _PlayTopOfDeck summons minions via Summon + manual Battlecry(card, None) and casts spells via CastSpellTargetsEnemiesIfPossible, rather than routing through the real Play pipeline. Consequences: OWN_MINION_PLAY / play-broadcast events do not fire, Combo is not triggered, and targeted battlecries are fired with target=None (so they pick no target).
real: Printed: 'At the end of your turn, play the top 3 cards from your deck.' A true 'play' fires play events, combos, and lets targeted battlecries choose a target. The impl is a close approximation but skips the full play-event broadcast and gives targeted battlecries no target.

issue: play = Draw(CONTROLLER).then(Buff(Draw.CARD,'EDR_234e2')) * 2. The 'can't play them for 2 turns' lockout is NOT modelled - EDR_234e2 (Still Growing) is applied as a purely cosmetic marker; the drawn cards are immediately playable.
real: Printed: 'Draw 2 cards. You can't play them for 2 turns.' Data enchant EDR_234e2 = 'Can't be played for 2 turns.' The 2-turn play-lock is a real gameplay downside that the engine has no lifetime mechanism for, so it is dropped.

issue: While in hand/deck, _WallowAbsorb scans each friendly field minion's `getattr(minion, "_dark_gifts", [])` list to copy Dark Gifts onto Wallow. But the actual Dark-Gift-granting action `_GiveDarkGift` in neutral.py applies gifts via `SetTags(t, tags)` and NEVER appends to any `_dark_gifts` list. `_dark_gifts` is referenced only in warlock.py and is written nowhere in the codebase (verified: after _GiveDarkGift runs, hasattr(minion,'_dark_gifts') is False). So the scan always sees an empty list and Wallow copies nothing - the card's entire effect is a dead no-op.
real: Printed: "While this is in your hand or deck, it gains a copy of every Dark Gift given to your minions." Wallow should accumulate the Dark Gift bonuses granted to your board minions while it sits in hand/deck.

issue: Battlecry play() iterates hand minions and only buffs (EDR_654e, COST -2) those where `getattr(card, "_dark_gifts", None)` is truthy. As with Wallow, nothing in the engine ever populates `_dark_gifts` (Dark Gifts are applied through SetTags, not by appending to that list). So the filter is always falsy and the battlecry reduces no costs - a dead no-op. (The EDR_654e enchant itself correctly carries COST: -2; the bug is the gating condition never matches.)
real: Printed: "Taunt. Battlecry: Reduce the Cost of minions in your hand with Dark Gifts by (2)." Hand minions that were granted a Dark Gift should get -2 cost. (Note: data enchant EDR_654e ships as '+5 Health' text but the impl overrides with COST -2, which matches the printed cost-reduction - that override is correct; the defect is the empty `_dark_gifts` gate.)

issue: play = DISCOVER(RandomMinion(deathrattle=True)) - Discovers a Deathrattle minion but does NOT restrict the pool to (or grant) a Dark Gift. The discovered minion never receives a Dark Gift. The class comment explicitly acknowledges the 'with a Dark Gift' attachment is unmodelled.
real: Printed: "Discover a Deathrattle minion with a Dark Gift." The discovered minion should arrive carrying a Dark Gift (a random Nightmare bonus). Other Dark-Gift discover cards in neutral.py do chain `.then(_GiveDarkGift(...))`; this one omits it entirely.

issue: Approximates 'next card costs OPPONENT'S Health instead of Mana' by (a) Refresh(FRIENDLY_HAND, {COST:-100}) to make the next card free, and (b) _AgamagganPay dealing `min(10, target.data.cost or 0)` to the enemy hero on the next OWN_CARD_PLAY. It bills the card's PRINTED base cost (`target.data.cost`), ignoring any cost reductions/increases the card actually had, and zeroes every hand card via the aura (not just the next one) until the next play fires. Net resource model (player pays nothing, opponent loses cost-in-health) is a reasonable stand-in but the magnitude can diverge from the card's real current cost.
real: Printed: "Battlecry: The next card you play costs your OPPONENT'S Health instead of Mana (up to 10)." The health spent should equal the card's actual cost (capped at 10), and only the single next card is affected.

issue: The ChooseBoth combined branch uses Destroy(RANDOM(ENEMY_MINIONS)) - a random enemy minion - for the destroy half, because ChooseBoth can't carry a target. The standalone EDR_490b correctly destroys a chosen TARGET. Only relevant when both halves fire together (Choose-Both effects); normal single-choice play is correct.
real: Printed: "Choose One - Summon two 3/6 Demons with Taunt that can't attack; or Destroy an enemy minion." The destroy half should target a chosen enemy minion; under a true Choose-Both it would destroy a (player-chosen) enemy minion rather than a random one.

issue: requirements only set REQ_TARGET_TO_PLAY / REQ_MINION_TARGET / REQ_FRIENDLY_TARGET, so the Location can choose ANY friendly minion, not just a Dragon. It is missing PlayReq.REQ_TARGET_WITH_RACE: Race.DRAGON (the established pattern, e.g. dragons/neutral_rare.py:41). _ClutchHatch stores source.target.id unconditionally, so a non-Dragon target would still hatch a copy of that non-Dragon minion.
real: Printed: '[x]Choose a friendly Dragon.\nSummon a 0/2 Egg that\nhatches into a copy of it.' The target must be restricted to friendly Dragons.

issue: The Horrible Egg's deathrattle resummons the chosen Dragon by bare id (egg._hatch_id = chosen.id; Summon(CONTROLLER, hatch_id)), producing a fresh base-stat minion. Any buffs/enchantments/Dark-Gift modifications on the chosen Dragon at the time of casting are lost.
real: Printed: 'Summon a 0/2 Egg that hatches into a copy of it.' A true copy should snapshot the current (buffed) stats/enchantments of the chosen Dragon, not just its base card id.

issue: Dark Gift is approximated. _DarkriderDiscover discovers a Dragon via RandomMinion(race=Race.DRAGON) then attaches a single representative +2/+2 enchant (EDR_456e, a @custom_card 'Dark Gift'). The real Dark Gift mechanic grants a RANDOM gift from the EDR_100t* pool of ~13 distinct transform/gift effects, not a fixed +2/+2.
real: Printed: 'Battlecry: If you're holding a Dragon, Discover a Dragon with a Dark Gift.' Dark Gift is a random one of the set's gift enchantments; the discover/HOLDING_DRAGON gate itself is implemented faithfully.
